review_text: This EWFEN sourdough starter kit is a really solid all-in-one set, with several pieces that are genuinely useful if you’re getting into sourdough baking.One of the best parts of the kit is the banneton proofing baskets. You get a 10” oval and a 9” round, both great sizes for medium loaves. They come with linen covers, care instructions, and a cleaning brush. You’re meant to dust them with flour before use and dry-brush them clean (no water), and with proper care they should last a long time.The sourdough starter jar is another standout. It has measurement markings, a built-in thermometer, and a rotating date band so you can track feedings — which is super helpful when maintaining a starter. It also includes a linen jar cover so the starter can breathe while fermenting.The kit includes recipes for baking sourdough bread, but it does NOT include instructions on how to actually make a sourdough starter, which feels like an odd omission for a “starter” kit. You’ll need to look up starter instructions separately.There’s also a silicone baking mat, measuring cups and spoons, a silicone spatula, and other kitchen tools. Some of these feel a bit lightweight and are items many people already own, but they’re still practical — especially the measuring cups, since you’ll use them frequently for feeding your starter. The spatula is a great shape for scraping the starter jar, though a bit short.A fun bonus is the bread decorating stencils and flour sifter — including a surprisingly funny pot leaf stencil.All in, this 25-piece kit is a convenient way to get started with sourdough. Aside from needing a covered cast iron bread pan (Dutch oven), it covers almost everything else. It would also make a great gift for anyone interested in baking.

review_text: I started my sourdough journey about 6 months ago and have been making changes to equipment and recipes constantly to find that sweet spot. This starter kit looked amazing for the price to have equipment to be used specifically for my sourdough baking.• Quality: There are a mixture of high quality, and mid quality items in this kit but overall, it gives you just about everything and more to get started. I am going to break this review down into parts since this kit includes so many things.Starter Jar: What I like about this jar is it is thick, heavy and tall. There are markings on the jar for measurements in ml, and a spot for marking when you last fed it. A rubber band is included with day and time (AM PM) that you can also use for making feedings. There is ample room for your starter to rise (I have a 100gram 6-month-old starter in the one in the images). What I do not like - because the jar is so tall, it‘s almost impossible to keep the sides of the jar clean and clear when feeding so you can see the activity of your starter. I previously used two, quart sized mason jars and will probably go back to that method. (using a clean jar at each feeding). There is a cloth lid included which I did not use. I personally like my loose saran wrap.Temperature tape: It is a great idea, but as shown in the images the tape included in my kit did not work. (I use a warmer which keeps my SD at the right temp)Measurement tools: The spoons and cups are cute. Not a high quality but being covered in a silicon covering it makes them easy to use and clean. Especially for SD.SD specific tools: The dough spatula is small and does not really work in the tall jar but is excellent in my quart jars. The Scandinavian dough tool is good quality and works as it should.The bannetons and tops are smaller than average size. But when you are just starting out, they are great to have and easy to use. Having the option of round or oval is a plus as well.The scoring templates are a very nice accessory; I have not used them as of yet but am looking forward to it.The dough scraper and cutter are nice, easy to use and clean.The silicone sling is again like the bannetons smaller than average size, and does not correctly fit my Dutch oven, but I have learned the slings are much easier to work with than parchment paper.The Lame is average and comes with a couple replacement blades which should last you years even if you become a daily baker.• Performance: Easy to work with kit that is excellent for starting out. The kit includes a small instruction book for how to use and care for your bannetons and lame, which is handy if you are a beginner. I love the additional bread bags and stickers as well. Easy to bag up and give your baked product to friends, family or neighbors.• Durability: If cared for this kit should last for years and allow a beginner to figure out what works and what doesn‘t in the SD journey and add to it as needed.Overall, I am very pleased with the kit and would recommend as an excellent value for the price. It would also make an excellent gift for someone who is thinking about getting into the SD culture.

Sometimes, two loaves will last a couple of weeks. Anyway, I always bake two loaves at a time since it‘s a couple of days process. One is usually unbleached white flour or whole wheat, and the second loaf is usually a seeded Rye. To keep them fresh, for years I reused plastic Dave’s bread bags, but honestly my loaves are big enough to make that a challenge. The bags were barely large enough. So I began looking for something better.At first I tried muslin bags,which while they are great for transporting bread, they are useless for keeping it fresh. The muslin being extremely porous, the bread dries out and gets stale very quickly.Luckily I found the Grin By Grin bags. They come as a pair which is perfect  for my needs.  Also, being different  colors ivory and blue I can easily distinguish one loaf from the other. I have used these bags continuously for about 13 months and they are great!Pros:They are very well made and sturdy.  I haven’t had a single issue in that regard. Complaints I’ve read about weak seams or zippers are definitely not true for me.They breath, but are not extremely porous, so they keep my bread fresh without it getting stale or drying out.They are large. In a couple of my pictures you can see that I easily fit two loaves onto a single bag.  I don’t do that, but I wanted to show it’s possible.The zipper is really not necessary as it’s really the rolling and buckling the end of the bag that seals it. I say that because a few of the complaints I read regarded the zipper failing.They claim to be machine washable, but I have not found it necessary and I don’t think I’d risk it. It’s so easy to shake out the crumbs and I’ve even turned them inside out at least once and wet wiped them.I’ve not had my bread mold in them and I’ve kept bread in them for up to two weeks. That said, I don’t even bag my bread until it’s 24 hours old and I refrigerate my bread after I bag it. Occasionally, if I know it will be a while before we consume it, I will freeze it.  These bags are great for either. I have seen a few complaints of moisture build up in the bags and mold occurring. I have experienced neither. I believe my success is because I never bag my bread until the day after it’s been baked and after that, I store it in the refrigerator.Cons: None!

review_text: First time using bees wax wrap and I’m sold! I bought the large size and ended up cutting it smaller. I got a bread maker for Christmas and I’ve been making bread almost every day since. I was very worried about freshness and keeping mold away because I live in a humid tropical climate. Store bought bread starts getting moldy within 3 days in their plastic if they’re sitting on the counter. Well, these wraps work! I really want my family to greatly reduce ultraprocessed foods and the plastic wraps they come in, and these wraps keep the bread mold-free AND soft like the day it was baked. The wraps are super easy to use, smell really nice, easy to clean with just a rinse (we use these only for homemade bread), and plenty large enough to fit a whole 2lb loaf. A few tips:
1. Let your bread cool COMPLETELY after baking. I usually wait over an hour, til the crust is COOL - not warm - COOL to the touch.
2. I slice up the bread and let them sit flat on a cooling rack to let any residual heat/moisture escape. Not sure how long, I usually go off and do something and then come back to it maybe 20-30 minutes later.
3. Stand the bread slices upright and make sure they fit back together right before wrapping. This keeps the crumb as moist as it needs to be while wrapped.
4. I wrap both ends, but unwrap only one end every time I need a slice just to make it easier to rewrap. I also grab slices from the middle and save the ends for last.
5. I keep them in a closed pantry in the kitchen, away from any heat sources or moisture. Definitely don’t keep it out on the counter next to the stove/air fryer/toaster/dishawasher/etc.

So far, my French bread has lasted 3 days, and my wheat/milk breads have lasted 4 days. The only reason I can’t vouch for longer than that is because my family eats it up by them. Although, based on the freshness up to the very last slice, I’m sure the bread is capable of lasting at least a couple more days beyond that. I will recommend these to everyone I know who bakes at home and will likely buy a few more for myself as I get more comfortable baking.

review_text: These bread bags are undeniably well made—durable stitching, functional zip closures, and a charming farmhouse aesthetic that elevates your countertop or lunch bag. They do a great job extending the freshness of foods (breads, produce, snacks), and they’re a solid upgrade from disposable plastic. That said, the environmental claims deserve a closer look. Marketing phrases like “eco-friendly,” “natural organic beeswax,” and “sustainable” are appealing—but in practice, these bags don’t fully align with zero-waste principles. The waxed lining doesn’t behave like traditional beeswax wraps—it lacks the distinct scent, texture, and pliability, and may include paraffin or other stabilizers (which aren’t compostable). And while the bags are reusable, their construction includes a zipper and plastic buckle—features that extend the product life and enhance utility, but also complicate end-of-life disposal. This isn’t a product you can toss in the compost when it’s worn out. In short: these bags are excellent for food storage, especially for short-term freshness. But for eco-conscious buyers expecting a fully recyclable or biodegradable option, this lands more in the “eco-inspired” category than truly “eco-friendly.” Still a great tool for reducing single-use waste, just know what you’re really getting.
